name: Johnny Cake
description: Historical recipe from Miss Leslie's Complete Cookery (1851). Source method; not modernized or kitchen-tested.

instructions.text: Sift a quart of Indian meal into a pan; make a hole in the middle, and pour in a pint of warm water.
Mix the meal and water gradually into a batter, adding a small tea-spoonful of salt.
Beat it very hard, and for a long time, till it becomes quite light.
Spread it thick and even on a stout piece of smooth board.
Place it upright on the hearth before a clear fire, with a flat iron or something of the sort to support the board behind, and bake it well.
Cut it into squares, and split and butter them hot.

source.author: Eliza Leslie
source.originalInstructions:
1. Sift a quart of Indian meal into a pan; make a hole in the middle, and pour in a pint of warm water.
2. Mix the meal and water gradually into a batter, adding a small tea-spoonful of salt.
3. Beat it very hard, and for a long time, till it becomes quite light.
4. Spread it thick and even on a stout piece of smooth board.
5. Place it upright on the hearth before a clear fire, with a flat iron or something of the sort to support the board behind, and bake it well.
6. Cut it into squares, and split and butter them hot.
